pains.title: Testing is paid for in hours before it is paid in cash
pains.problem: A testing episode runs through intake, scoring and report writing before the claim goes out. Clinicians are paid every payroll, while cash arrives weeks later.
pains.how: Lucid tracks testing as its own revenue line, keeps deposits apart from insurance receivables and forecasts the gap before payroll. Lucid works alongside your biller.

pains.title: Not knowing whether testing or therapy makes money
pains.problem: Therapy, testing, forensic and school work run side by side, on different codes and with different staff. Without separate books, you cannot tell which line funds the others.
pains.how: Lucid tags revenue, clinician pay, technician pay and test materials to each line, then reports profit by service line and margin by clinician each month.

pains.title: Hiring psychometrists and postdocs
pains.problem: Whether technician or pre licensed work can be billed under a supervisor differs by payer and state. That decides how much revenue each hire can generate.
pains.how: Lucid models the fully loaded cost of each hire against revenue actually collected, with a ramp period. Billing rules are a question for your biller and counsel.

faq.q: Why is my psychology practice profitable on paper but always short on cash?
faq.a: Testing work is paid for in clinician and technician hours weeks before the final claim is billed and paid. Lucid's cash flow forecast shows the gap before payroll, with testing tracked as its own revenue line.

faq.q: How do I know if psychological testing is more profitable than therapy in my group practice?
faq.a: You need your income and costs split by service line, including the unpaid report writing time. Lucid sets up your books that way and sends a monthly report showing margin for testing, therapy and any contract work, so you can decide where to add clinicians or technicians.

faq.q: Which insurance companies actually pay well for psychological testing?
faq.a: Rates for the same testing codes vary a lot by payer and by contract. Lucid's payer mix tracking shows what each payer pays, and your biller handles the claims, so you can decide which panels are worth keeping.

faq.q: Does it make financial sense to hire a psychometrist or a postdoc?
faq.a: It depends on how much revenue each person generates after supervision time, payroll taxes and benefits, and on whether your payers allow the billing. Lucid models the cost and the collected revenue per hire from your own numbers, so you see how many months until the hire pays for themselves.

faq.q: Should my psychology group pay clinicians as employees or contractors, and what split is sustainable?
faq.a: Lucid compares the real cost of each setup for every role and shows what each split leaves for the owner. Lucid's classification review flags risks to raise with your attorney. Lucid does not give legal advice.
